questions.q: What does Journal Import actually do?
options: Posts already-existing journals to the ledger
Reconciles bank statements
Reads rows from GL_INTERFACE (often fed by an external system) and turns them into actual GL journals
Builds payment files for suppliers
questions.explain: Journal Import is the step before posting: it converts interface table rows into actual journal entries in General Ledger.

questions.q: What does error code EF04 mean during Journal Import?
options: The journal is unbalanced
The account is disabled
Suspense posting was used
The account combination is invalid
questions.explain: EF04 specifically indicates the account is invalid — the combination doesn't exist or fails cross-validation.

questions.q: What does it mean when 'dynamic insertion' is turned off for a ledger?
options: Journal Import will reject a row whose account combination doesn't already exist, rather than creating it
Journal Import will automatically create any missing account combination
All journals automatically post without review
The ledger cannot accept any new journals
questions.explain: With dynamic insertion off, Journal Import will not create a new account combination on the fly — it rejects rows referencing one that doesn't already exist.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of all 60 rows failing at Harbor & Vance Logistics?
options: The accounting period was closed
The legacy payroll system sent a new department/cost-center segment value that had never been created in GL's chart of accounts
All 60 journals were unbalanced
The GL_INTERFACE table was corrupted
questions.explain: Payroll began using a new cost center value on its end that was never communicated to or set up in GL, so none of the 60 rows could find a valid matching account combination.

questions.q: Why was simply turning on dynamic insertion not the recommended fix here?
options: Dynamic insertion cannot be turned on in Oracle Fusion
It would have taken longer than manually creating the account
For a cost center, auto-creating the combination risked creating an incomplete or incorrectly structured value instead of one with proper parent/rollup behavior
It would have required a system outage
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a new cost center should be created deliberately through Enterprise Structures to ensure correct structure, rather than relying on automatic creation.
